history.period: 1058 CE (18th regnal year of Udyotakesari; some sources give 1060 CE — verify)
history.summary: The Brahmeswara Temple in Bhubaneswar's Old Town is a milestone of mature Kalinga architecture, dated by temple inscriptions (now lost, but recorded) to the 18th regnal year of Somavamsi king Udyotakesari — about 1058 CE — when it was built by his mother, Queen Kolavati Devi, at Siddhatirtha in Ekamra (modern Bhubaneswar). A panchayatana complex with four corner shrines, its sandstone vimana rises about 60 ft with a curvilinear shikhara. It shows strong affinity with the earlier Mukteswara Temple (lion-head motifs in profusion, carved jagamohana interior) while introducing innovations: crowds of musicians and dancers on the exterior walls, tantric imagery including Chamunda on the western facade, and — per architectural sources — the first use of iron beams in an Odisha temple. The sanctum holds a black-stone Shiva linga. Note: one inscription carried to Calcutta is dated to Udyotakesari's 18th year as 1060 CE and scholars caution it may reference a different temple, so the 1058 vs 1060 dating should be treated as (verify). CSV town and state (Bhubaneswar, Odisha) are correct; district is Khurda.

name: Brahmeswara Temple
town_description: Bhubaneswar, the capital of Odisha, is called the 'City of Temples' and Ekamra Kshetra, with a temple-building history stretching back over two millennia. The Old Town clusters the great Kalinga temples — Lingaraja, Ananta Vasudeva, Brahmeswara, Mukteswara, Rajarani — around the sacred Bindu Sagar tank; the modern city also hosts the Dhauli Shanti Stupa and the Udayagiri-Khandagiri Jain caves nearby.
